notes: Source: Blackmagic Design's own official Product Technical Specifications sheet (verified verbatim via a hosted PDF mirror at cpl.tech, content and layout identical to blackmagicdesign.com/products/multiview/techspecs) plus the Blackmagic MultiView installation/operation manual for connector confirmation. Connections per the official rear-panel diagram: 16x SDI In (SD/HD/3G/6G-SDI, auto-switching), 16x SDI Loop Out (reclocked loop-through of each input, same auto-switching rate), 2x HD-SDI multiview out, 2x 6G-SDI multiview out, 1x HDMI type A multiview out, REF In (Black Burst/Tri-Sync), RS-422 Remote, RJ45 Ethernet, USB (2.0, 480Mb/s), and an IEC AC power inlet (90-240V, 45W). 1RU, less than 6in deep, 2.3kg. Caveats: (1) the RS-422 port's physical connector is called "RJ9" on Blackmagic's own spec-sheet diagram but "RJ11" in the full manual text — neither exists in the allowed connector list, so it is mapped to the closest id, rs422; (2) the USB port's physical shape (Type B vs Micro-USB) is not stated in any Blackmagic document found; Type B was assumed and should be verified against the physical unit if precision matters; (3) HDMI version (1.4/2.0) is never stated by Blackmagic, so grade is omitted on that port; (4) Ethernet link speed is never stated (control/config only, no video), so grade is omitted; (5) this is the original/discontinued HDL-MULTIP6G/16 model — Blackmagic has since released newer multiview products, so verify part number if sourcing a currently-shipping unit.

ports.name: HDMI Out
ports.note: HDMI type A multiview (mosaic) output; auto-detects monitor EDID and switches between HD/Ultra HD. Blackmagic does not publish an HDMI version number for this port, so no grade is set.

ports.name: REF In
ports.note: Reference sync input, Black Burst or Tri-level sync for SD/HD/4K; not a data-bearing SDI grade so no grade is set.

ports.name: RS-422 Remote
ports.note: For third-party router/automation control. Blackmagic's own marketing spec sheet diagram labels this connector "RJ9" while the full installation manual describes it as an RJ11 (6P4C phone-style) jack; neither RJ9 nor RJ11 exists in the connector list, so it is mapped to the closest available id, rs422.

ports.name: Ethernet
ports.note: For IP configuration, firmware updates, and Blackmagic Videohub Ethernet control protocol. Used for control only, not video transport; Blackmagic does not publish a link speed for this port so no grade is set.

ports.name: USB
ports.note: USB 2.0 High Speed (480Mb/s), used with Blackmagic MultiView Setup software for firmware updates and IP address configuration. Blackmagic's documentation does not show the physical USB connector shape (Type B vs Micro-USB); Type B is assumed based on typical Blackmagic hardware of this generation and is unconfirmed.

ports.name: Power Connector
ports.note: IEC power cable required, 90-240V AC input, 45W consumption.
